newsitem.title: GERMANY: Deutsche Telekom sees higher first half 1997 profits.
newsitem.headline: Deutsche Telekom sees higher first half 1997 profits.

text.p: Deutsche Telekom chief financial officer Joachim Kroeske said he saw profit in the first half of 1997 above that of the second half of 1996 because of the lack of flotation-related expenses and lower interest payments.
"Profit in the first half of 1997 will be much better than that seen in the second half of 1996," Kroeske told journalists after a speech to a financial conference in Frankfurt on Thursday.
He also said that the group aimed to publish quarterly results in accordance with U.S. GAAP accountancy standards.
Kroeske said there were no plans to increase dividend payments of 1.20 marks per share announced at the time of the company's massive flotation in November.
He said, however, that dividends in following years would rise if earnings increase.
"We have forecast earnings increases," said Kroeske. Telekom has said that it plans to pay out between 50 and 60 percent of its profits in dividends.
On the company's massive debt, which was 82 billion marks ($48.56 billion) at the end of 1996, Kroeske said that this would fall to clearly below 80 billion marks in 1997.

Current forecasts at Deutsche Telekom are for operating profit of over six billion marks on turnover of 63 billion marks. In the first half of 1996 earnings were 2.7 billion marks. Kroeske promised to present more detailed figures at the Cebit fair in Hanover in March. ($1=1.6886 Mark)
